overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's rethinking of phenomenological method. You'll be asked about the four themes of the Preface, operative intentionality, the incomplete reduction, and the meaning of the primacy of perception.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why, on Merleau-Ponty's account, can the reduction never be completed?

options.html: Because philosophers lack the training to perform it fully
options.text: Because philosophers lack the training to perform it fully
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The problem isn't training. The one who reflects remains rooted in the world the reduction tries to bracket.

options.html: Because the one who reflects remains rooted in the world
options.text: Because the one who reflects remains rooted in the world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Reflection is itself in the world, in a body and in time, so it can't cut the ties it makes visible.

options.html: Because the world may not exist, so there's nothing to reduce
options.text: Because the world may not exist, so there's nothing to reduce
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The reduction doesn't doubt the world. It can't be completed because the reflecting subject remains rooted in the world.

options.html: Because Husserl never explained how to perform it
options.text: Because Husserl never explained how to perform it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty's point is about our being-in-the-world, not about Husserl's instructions.

forms.stemHtml: Before you decide anything about it, a hillside path shows up as inviting to walk. Which kind of intentionality is at work?

options.html: Act intentionality, since you judge the path to be walkable
options.text: Act intentionality, since you judge the path to be walkable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No explicit judgment has been made. The path's invitation is given pre-reflectively, which is operative intentionality.
Correct! Operative intentionality establishes the world's meaning before any explicit act.

options.html: Reflective analysis, since the mind constructs the path
options.text: Reflective analysis, since the mind constructs the path
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Reflective analysis is a method Merleau-Ponty rejects. The invitation is given through operative intentionality.

options.html: No intentionality, since nothing is being thought
options.text: No intentionality, since nothing is being thought
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Intentionality doesn't require explicit thought. Operative intentionality is pre-reflective.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are among the Preface's claims about phenomenology? (Select all that apply.)

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Phenomenology describes how things are given rather than explaining them by causes.

options.html: Essences are a means, not the goal
options.text: Essences are a means, not the goal
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Essences help describe the meaning experience already has.

options.html: The reduction loosens our ties without cutting them
options.text: The reduction loosens our ties without cutting them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The reduction loosens the intentional threads to make them visible.

options.html: It's reflective analysis of a constituting mind
options.text: It's reflective analysis of a constituting mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty sets phenomenology against reflective analysis.

options.html: It proves that the world doesn't exist
options.text: It proves that the world doesn't exist
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Phenomenology suspends belief in the world without denying it.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's image for the ties that bind perceiver to world, which the reduction loosens to make visible but can't cut? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The reduction slackens the intentional threads, bringing them into view, but can't break them.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty's image is the intentional threads.

forms.stemHtml: What does Merleau-Ponty mean by the "primacy of perception"?

options.html: That everything, including numbers, is really a perception
options.text: That everything, including numbers, is really a perception
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thesis isn't that everything is perception. It's that knowledge, reason, and value presuppose the perceived world.

options.html: That perception is always more accurate than thought
options.text: That perception is always more accurate than thought
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thesis is about foundation, not accuracy.

options.html: That all knowledge presupposes the perceived world
options.text: That all knowledge presupposes the perceived world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Science, logic, and ethics arise from and depend on a world first given in perception.

options.html: That only perceptual beliefs can be called true
options.text: That only perceptual beliefs can be called true
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The thesis doesn't restrict truth to perception. It says knowledge presupposes the perceived world.

title: The Unfinished Reduction
